newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian parliament sacks Savings Bank head.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian parliament sacks Savings Bank head.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament dismissed on Friday the chairman of State Savings Bank (SSB), which is investigated by the security service over its alleged illegal operations.
"The government proposed to relieve (Bistra) Dimitrova of her duties on grounds of damaging the reputation and stability of the SSB," Finance Minister Muravei Radev told parliament.
The motion was supported by 154 deputies, 47 voted against and seven abstained of the 240-seat assembly.
Parliament appointed as her successor Spas Dimitrov, a lawyer and former deputy of the ruling Union of Democratic Forces (UDF).
The UDF leader Ivan Kostov made clear he would seek Dimitrova's dismissal immediately after being appointed Prime Minister last week.

The National Security Service launched an investigation of SSB earlier this week after receiving signals of illegally transferred funds from the SSB to several private commercial banks. No more details of the allegations were available.
Dimitrova's appointment as a SSB chairman in June 1995 sparked heated debates in the previous Socialist-dominated parliament.
Deputies from the UDF, then in opposition, alleged that she was linked to powerful private business conglomerates.
The SSB operates under a special law which bans from operating in foreign currency allowing it to perform most banking activities. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
